headline: PAGASA Places Zambales, Bataan and Other Central Luzon Areas Under Orange Rainfall Warning
seoTitle: Orange Rainfall Warning for Parts of Central Luzon | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA placed Zambales, Tarlac, Bataan, Pampanga and parts of Bulacan under an Orange rainfall warning at 5 a.m. on August 28 due to Habagat.
deck: PAGASA said flooding was threatening in Orange-warning areas as the southwest monsoon continued to bring heavy rain across parts of Central Luzon.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA placed Zambales, Tarlac, Bataan, Pampanga and specified areas of Bulacan under an Orange rainfall warning at 5 a.m. Friday, August 28, because of the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat.

The weather bureau said flooding was threatening in the Orange-warning areas. Metro Manila, parts of Nueva Ecija and other areas of Bulacan were under a Yellow warning, where flooding was possible in flood-prone communities.

sections.heading: Warning versus rainfall outlook
paragraphs: The 5 a.m. warning was a short-fuse alert based on observed and expected rain over the next several hours. It is separate from PAGASA's multi-day heavy-rainfall outlook, which projected 100 to 200 millimeters over several western Luzon provinces during parts of the weekend.
The distinction matters because warning levels and covered municipalities may change more quickly than the broader multi-day outlook.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: A low-pressure area east of Northern Luzon was also being monitored and had a medium chance of developing into a tropical cyclone within 48 hours, according to PAGASA-attributed reporting. Forecasters said it could strengthen the Habagat even if it did not make landfall.
The disturbance's development and track remained uncertain at the time of publication. Hazardous monsoon rain can continue independently of whether it becomes a named storm.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated rain has increased flood and landslide risks in vulnerable communities. PAGASA advised the public and local disaster offices to monitor conditions and follow succeeding warnings.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PAGASA scheduled the next rainfall-warning update for 8 a.m. Residents should rely on the latest official warning, river-basin advisory and local disaster-office instruction because affected areas and warning levels can change rapidly.
